newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori flies to thank pope over hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori flies to thank pope over hostages.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori left for Rome on Friday to thank Pope John Paul for his help during Peru's four-month crisis when Marxist rebels held 72 hostages.

Fujimori flew out of Lima with a delegation of 46 people including former captives and the bereaved relatives of a hostage and two commandos, who died during the military's April 22 rescue strike at the Japanese ambassador's home.
Fujimori will meet on Monday with the pope and Italy's President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro before returning on Tuesday to Peru, which has more than 21 million Roman Catholics.
The president, who had surgery last month to remove a tumour in his mouth, also travelled with a doctor and nurse from the cancer hospital where he was operated on.
During the hostage siege the Vatican provided Peruvian Archbishop Luis Cipriani as a mediator to oversee talks between the government and Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.
But his work was ultimately fruitless as Fujimori ordered troops to storm the diplomatic compound in a bloody raid that killed all 14 hostage-takers.

The violent end was also potentially embarrassing for the Vatican as the assault was launched with a tip-off via a microphone planted in a crucifix that had been smuggled into the residence, military sources said.

The pope has first-hand knowledge of the Peruvian guerrillas' work after an episode in 1990 when the larger Maoist Shining Path group coordinated an electricity blackout in the whole of Lima to coincide with the religious leader's landing in the capital on a visit.
